locator.section: 8.x Proton-bound complexes / hydrogen rearrangement (rH) in even-electron ions

evidence.curator_note: EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXT: metastable-ion (MI) decomposition of the mass-selected even-electron ion C2H5O+=CH2 (m/z 59). The book (eq 8.14) DRAWS a proton-bound complex [C2H4...H...O=CH2] as the intermediate; it is a non-covalent complex and is NOT separately encoded as a discrete mapped species (partial bonds are not RDKit-representable) - this record encodes the net rH reaction precursor->products. The MI spectrum shows HO-CH2+ as a major peak (this channel). 0 electron-pushing arcs drawn (only 'rH' reaction arrows). Equation 8.14, favored (upper) branch. The even-electron oxocarbenium ion C2H5-O+=CH2 (ethyl methyleneoxocarbenium, m/z 59) rearranges by rH (labelled 'rH' on the reaction arrow) to a proton-bound complex [C2H4...H...O=CH2]+ (drawn as an explicit intermediate on the page) that dissociates to neutral ethylene C2H4 + protonated formaldehyde HO+=CH2 (the hydroxymethyl cation, m/z 31). The text states this HO-CH2+ 'represents a major peak' in the MI spectrum of C2H5O=CH2+ and that no C2H5+ is seen. INTERMEDIATE OMITTED: the drawn proton-bound complex is a non-covalent ion-neutral complex, not cleanly representable as a covalent SMILES with defined bond orders, so this record encodes the NET rearrangement (precursor -> C2H4 + HO+=CH2) as a single formal-arrow step; this matches the granularity of MOD rule IMS_8_14_2. Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs (a reaction-level scheme using reaction arrows labelled rH); both encoded moves are reconstructed for electron balance (not drawn on the page): move <1> routes the C1-H4 sigma pair (a beta H of the ethyl group) into the forming C1=C5 pi bond of ethylene, move <2> routes the C5-O8 sigma pair into the new O8-H4 bond of protonated formaldehyde. A 1,4-hydrogen shift (H-C1-C5-O8) through a 4-membered transfer array; closed-shell throughout (no radicals). The reaction is drawn as an equilibrium (reversible=true).

Cross-linked MOD rules for equation 8.14 (rule_index by_equation['8.14'] = IMS_8_14_1, IMS_8_14_1b, IMS_8_14_2). IMS_8_14_2 is the match for THIS favored branch: its DFS is [C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11) >> [C]1([H]2)([H]3)[C]5([H]6)([H]7) . [H]4[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11) -- same precursor C2H5O+=CH2, same bond changes (C5-O8 cleaved, H4 transferred from C1 to O8) and mass/charge (C3H7O+ -> C2H4 + CH3O+). CAVEAT (bond order): IMS_8_14_2 leaves the ethylene fragment C1-C5 as a SINGLE bond (no {=}), i.e. it does NOT form the C=C pi bond and encodes ethylene as a valence-incomplete/biradical CH2-CH2; my record forms the correct closed-shell CH2=CH2. Listed in rule_mismatches. IMS_8_14_1 and IMS_8_14_1b (the proton-bound-complex forward/back rH rules) are BROKEN: their product half was copy-pasted from IMS_8_13 (it carries an extra methyl carbon C11), so IMS_8_14_1 maps C3H7O+ -> C4H9O+ and IMS_8_14_1b maps C4H9O+ -> C3H7O+ -- neither conserves atoms, and both would be dropped by the conservation guardrail. Listed in rule_mismatches.

observed_mz 31.0173 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of HO+=CH2 (CH3O+, electron-mass corrected). The page (Eq 8.14 figure) prints NO m/z and NO percentage; the surrounding text merely calls HO-CH2+ 'a major peak'. status 'inferred', relative_intensity omitted (no printed intensity).
